paper_metadata.title: The Disability Rate of 5-Year Post-Stroke and Its Correlation Factors: A National Survey in China

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a large multicenter sample with clear inclusion criteria. However, the exclusion of patients unable to complete interviews at baseline and the significant differences between participants and non-participants (age and marital status) introduce a moderate risk of selection bias.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: At baseline, patients in 56 hospitals nationwide were consecutively recruited and enrolled if they were aged 18 years or older, had an acute stroke according to WHO criteria [11] confirmed by CT or MRI within 14 days
items.reasoning: The source population is clearly defined as acute ischemic stroke patients across 56 hospitals in China.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: At baseline, patients in 56 hospitals nationwide were consecutively recruited
items.reasoning: Consecutive recruitment across multiple sites helps limit selection bias.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The specific calendar dates for the baseline recruitment period are not explicitly stated in the text.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location) are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: 56 hospitals nationwide [China]
items.reasoning: The setting is clearly defined as a national hospital-based survey in China.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: enrolled if they were aged 18 years or older, had an acute stroke according to WHO criteria [11] confirmed by CT or MRI within 14 days... Patients with severe cognitive impairment and history of drug dependence were excluded.
items.reasoning: Criteria are explicit, including the 'zero time' (within 14 days of stroke).

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: patients who could not complete a clinical interview were excluded at baseline, which could lead to potential selection bias.
items.reasoning: The authors admit that excluding those unable to interview at baseline may bias the sample, and the initial participation rate of all eligible patients is not fully detailed.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Table 1 shows the basic demographic and clinical characteristics of the whole sample
items.reasoning: Comprehensive baseline data including age, sex, NIHSS, and comorbidities are provided.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: There is a very high attrition rate (only 38.4% of the baseline sample was analyzed). Furthermore, there are significant differences between completers and non-completers (age), which the authors acknowledge likely leads to an underestimation of the disability rate.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: Out of 2,324 ischemic stroke patients who fulfilled study entry criteria at baseline... Finally, data on 893 patients were included in the statistical analyses
items.reasoning: A follow-up rate of 38.4% is well below the standard 80% threshold for low risk.

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out
items.prompt: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out of the study are described.
items.evidence_snippet: 696 could not be located via the information recorded in medical records, and 474 refused or did not complete the telephone interview
items.reasoning: The reasons for dropout are categorized, but specific 'attempts' to re-engage or find them are not detailed beyond the mention of telephone interviews.

items.label: Reasons and potential impact of subjects lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Reasons for loss to follow-up are provided.
items.evidence_snippet: 248 died, 696 could not be located... 474 refused or did not complete the telephone interview
items.reasoning: Reasons are clearly quantified.

items.label: Outcome and prognostic factor information on those lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Participants lost to follow-up are adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Compared to patients who completed the 5-year assessment, those who were excluded for any reasons were older and more likely to be single marital status (S1 Table).
items.reasoning: The authors compared baseline characteristics of completers vs. non-completers.

items.prompt: There are no important differences between key characteristics (LIST) and outcomes in participants who completed the study and those who did not.
items.evidence_snippet: those who were excluded for any reasons were older... the prevalence rate in our study could be an under-estimation.
items.reasoning: Significant differences in age exist, which is a primary driver of the outcome (disability).

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Prognostic factors were measured using validated, standardized scales (NIHSS, MMSE, DSM-IV) by qualified professionals, and the measurement methods were consistent across the cohort.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Stroke severity was assessed at baseline by the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS)... Cognition function was measured by the Mini Mental State Examination (MMSE)
items.reasoning: All prognostic factors (NIHSS, MMSE, HRSD) are clearly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: supplemented by medical records review and a clinical interview by qualified neurologists... standardized instruments
items.reasoning: Validated scales were used and administered by trained neurologists.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: Cognitive impairment was defined as the MMSE total score < 24 [17, 18].
items.reasoning: The cut-point for MMSE is based on established literature, not data-driven.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Basic sociodemographic, clinical and neuro-imaging features at baseline were recorded using a standard form
items.reasoning: Standardized forms and protocols were used across all 56 sites.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: missing data in several variables... percentages of less than 0.5%, except for hyperlipidemia (1.5%).
items.reasoning: Missing data for the analyzed sample was very low.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: due to significant missing data of medication used, this was not included for analyses.
items.reasoning: The study excluded variables with high missingness rather than using imputation.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While the mRS is a standard tool, it was assessed via telephone interview at 5 years, which relies on self-report or proxy-report and may be less accurate than in-person clinical assessment.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Post-stroke functional status was assessed using the modified Ranking Score (mRS), with a score ≥ 2 as meeting the criteria for disability
items.reasoning: The outcome and its threshold are clearly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: The 5-year assessments including stroke recurrence and physical disability were conducted via a telephone interview.
items.reasoning: Telephone administration of mRS is common but carries a higher risk of misclassification than in-person assessment.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The 5-year assessments... were conducted via a telephone interview.
items.reasoning: All participants were assessed via the same telephone method.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study adjusted for many clinical and demographic factors. However, the authors acknowledge that key variables like rehabilitation therapy and infarct size were not included in the model due to unavailable data, which are significant potential confounders.

items.label: Important Confounders Measured
items.prompt: All important confounders, including treatments (key variables in conceptual model: LIST), are measured.
items.evidence_snippet: several important variables, such as post-stroke rehabilitation therapy, treatment adherence and the size of infarcts... were not evaluated
items.reasoning: Major confounders like rehabilitation and infarct size were missing.

items.label: Definition of the confounding factor
items.prompt: Clear definitions of the important confounders measured are provided (e.g., including dose, level, and duration of exposures).
items.evidence_snippet: Current smoking was defined as at least 1 cigarette in the past month. Moderate/heavy drinking was defined as 2 standard drinks/day.
items.reasoning: Confounders that were measured were well-defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders
items.prompt: Measurement of all important confounders is adequately valid and reliable (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: standardized instruments... medical records review
items.reasoning: Measurements used standard clinical definitions and records.

items.label: Method and Setting of Confounding Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of confounding measurement are the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: recorded using a standard form
items.reasoning: Consistency was maintained across the study population.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods are used if imputation is used for missing confounder data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: No imputation was performed; missing data resulted in exclusion of variables.

items.label: Appropriate Accounting for Confounding
items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the study design (e.g., matching for key variables, stratification, or initial assembly of comparable groups).
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The study was a prospective cohort without matching or stratification at design.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).
items.evidence_snippet: Multiple logistic regression analysis used the "enter" method... adjusting for study site
items.reasoning: Multivariable adjustment was performed for significant univariate factors and study site.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical methods are appropriate for the study design. The authors used multivariable logistic regression and reported both ORs and 95% CIs. They were transparent about the limitations and the high dropout rate.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: Statistical analysis included chi-square tests, two independent samples t-tests, Mann-Whitney U test and multiple logistic regression analysis.
items.reasoning: The analytical plan is clearly described.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: determine the independent relationships between disability at 5 years follow up and variables that significantly differed in the above univariate analysis.
items.reasoning: A standard univariate-to-multivariate approach was used.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: Multiple logistic regression analysis used the "enter" method
items.reasoning: Logistic regression is appropriate for the binary outcome (mRS <2 vs >=2).

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: Table 2 shows the independent correlates of disability
items.reasoning: All variables entered into the model are reported with their significance levels and effect sizes.
